prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_A:
Summary of proposals (non-ideological)

Health and care
- NHS: Extra revenue funding rising from £8bn in year one to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Targets include faster GP access, same‑day urgent GP access, guaranteed NHS dentistry, a National Cancer Plan, and 28‑day access to evidence‑based mental health therapies. £1.5bn public health uplift; primary care: +£1.5bn/year by 2030 and £2bn capital. Dentistry: +£3bn/year by 2030 and a new NHS contract. School counsellor in every school. Support for assisted dying (with safeguards). Aim to end new HIV transmissions by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year investment; national career structure and better pay; reforms to protect overseas care workers; “Care Supporter” right. Disability: immediate 5% benefit uplift; oppose replacing PIP cash with vouchers; SEND travel support. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils.

Homes and planning
- 150,000 new social homes/year; end no‑fault evictions; empower local rent controls; end “right to buy.” New homes to Passivhaus‑equivalent with solar and low‑carbon heat; upgrade PRS to EPC C. Retrofit programme: £29bn home insulation, £4bn public buildings insulation, £9bn low‑carbon heating, £7bn heat-resilience (five‑year totals). Bring empty homes into use; stronger local planning, lower embodied carbon, reuse demolition materials; reduce car dependence.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting ~£120/tCO2, rising to up to £500/t within 10 years. Wind to ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; lift onshore wind constraints; minimum community ownership share; expand grid, storage, interconnectors; green hydrogen for industry. Stop new nuclear and phase out existing stations.

Economy, taxation, and public ownership
- Green transition investment averaging £40bn/year (power, retrofits, rail, active travel, industry, water/sewage). Bring rail, water, and major retail energy suppliers into public ownership. Wealth tax: 1% on assets >£10m, 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension relief. Higher windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT cuts for hospitality/arts and rises for private education/financial services. Council tax revaluation and steps toward land value taxation. Regional mutual banks (+£10bn capital). R&D +£30bn over five years. Estimated additional annual receipts by end of parliament: personal/wealth £50–70bn; carbon tax up to ~£80bn; business taxes +£40bn over five years. Borrowing to invest within inflation constraints.

Work and incomes
- Charter of Workers’ Rights; repeal recent restrictions on industrial action; minimum wage £15/hour (all ages) with support for SMEs; 10:1 pay ratio cap; day‑one rights; gig workers classed as “workers”; safe sick pay; progress toward a four‑day week. Welfare: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; 5% disability uplift; carers’ allowance +10%; protect pension uprating; end sanctions; long‑term move to Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% of land and sea by 2030; public ownership of water; DEFRA +£1.5bn; Right to Roam Act; peat re‑wetting; fully protected MPAs; ban destructive fishing in MPAs. Animal Protection Commission; ban blood sports; end factory‑farming cages/routine antibiotics; end badger cull. Nearly triple farm support; cut pesticides; boost horticulture; free school meals for all children and breakfast clubs; local food partnerships and waste reduction.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/year to fix unsafe buildings; SEND +£5bn; counsellors and school nurses restored; reduce high‑stakes testing; Natural History GCSE; bring academies under local control; charge VAT on private school fees. Early years: Sure Start +£1.4bn/year; extend funded childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months. Post‑16/FE: sixth‑form +£3bn; FE skills +£12bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees and restore grants.

Transport
- Raise public transport subsidies to £10bn/year; +£19bn over five years for public transport, electrification, and active travel; public ownership of rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycling/walking. Oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; develop road pricing; ICE sales end by 2027, road use by 2035; EV scrappage rising to £5bn/year; more HGV rail freight. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; tax kerosene; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, digital, justice, foreign policy
- Proportional representation; votes at 16; elected second chamber; scrap voter ID; tighter lobbying/think‑tank transparency; expand devolution; defend Human Rights Act; repeal recent protest‑curbing laws; self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration/asylum: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work while claims processed; remove spousal income rules; simplify visas; free NHS for visa holders; voting rights for visa‑holding residents; create a Department of Migration.
- Arts/media/digital: £5bn over five years for local arts/sport; VAT exemption for cultural events; media ownership cap (≤20% per market); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation and creator IP protection.
- Justice/policing: restore trust, end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; domestic abuse priority; decriminalise sex work; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; expand diversion and restorative justice; invest ~£11bn over parliament in courts/legal aid/judges.
- International: support Ukraine; aim to rejoin EU (steps: customs union, free movement, Erasmus); sign the UN nuclear ban treaty, cancel Trident; NATO reform (no first use). Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; debt relief; support ecocide law. Israel–Palestine: immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognition of Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, war‑crimes investigations.

TEXT_D:
Summary of key proposals (non-exhaustive)

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self-employed NI during the next Parliament.
- Maintain rates of income tax and VAT; introduce a “Triple Lock Plus” so the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation, or 2.5%.
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; move Child Benefit to a household test starting taper at £120,000.
- Business: retain full expensing (explore extension to leasing), no rise in corporation tax, 10-point SME plan (business rates relief focus, prompt payments, Open Finance, regional mutual banks, keep key investment incentives).
- Regulation/Whitehall: reduce civil service to pre-pandemic size; halve spend on consultants; relocate roles out of London; expand digital/AI capability; Minimum Service Levels on strikes.

Infrastructure, innovation and trade
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 Phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, bus), including Northern Powerhouse Rail (Manchester–Liverpool) and Midlands Rail Hub; electrify North Wales Main Line.
- Nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; legal framework for automated vehicles; aviation SAF support; maritime connectivity review.
- R&D to £22bn/year; invest in compute for AI; advanced manufacturing plan; maintain R&D tax reliefs; support financial services competitiveness.
- Trade: implement CPTPP; pursue FTAs with India and GCC; deepen EU TCA without ceding sovereignty; maintain standards in NHS and food.

Education, skills and youth
- Ban mobile phones in school day; give parents access to curriculum materials; protect per-pupil funding in real terms.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19 (broader study, English and maths to 18).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor-outcome degree courses.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or part-time civic service).

Welfare and work
- Tighten work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes via specialist teams; reform PIP with greater focus on needs and treatment access; stronger sanctions for long-term non-compliance; fraud bill to bolster DWP powers.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First, modernise GP premises, add 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade: NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, data platforms; reduce managers by 5,500.
- Dental recovery plan (more NHS appointments, contract reform, rural “golden hellos”, vans); require new dentists to serve in NHS for a period or repay training.
- Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions (maternity safety, pelvic health, hubs); implement Cass Review; single-sex accommodation rights; expand youth/adult mental health access.

Borders, security and defence
- Legal annual cap on work/family migration that falls each year; raise salary thresholds; health checks and higher charges; restrict dependants; increase visa fees; expand returns deals.
- Monthly removals to Rwanda; seek international asylum reform; intensify organised immigration crime action.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; Defence Innovation Agency with 5% of budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; sustained support to Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and benefits.

Policing, justice, and civic order
- 8,000 additional neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; facial recognition and anti-knife powers; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences for serious offenders; four new prisons; more foreign offender removals; expand fraud measures.
- New protest controls (e.g., face coverings bans, cumulative impact); protect schools from targeted protests; counter-extremism measures.

Energy, climate and environment
- Annual North Sea oil/gas licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; two CCS clusters now and more later; expedite small modular reactors and approve Wylfa; expand interconnectors.
- Keep energy price cap; review standing charges; energy-efficiency vouchers and £6bn for home upgrades; onshore wind with local consent; solar away from best farmland; no fracking.
- Environment: deliver biodiversity targets, expand Blue Belt, moratorium on deep-sea mining, strengthen water regulation and penalties, river restoration fund, tree planting and urban greening, tougher fly-tipping penalties, deposit return scheme, limit new incinerators.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes in England; lift nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; fast-track brownfield; densify inner London; protect Green Belt.
- Permanent SDLT relief for first-time buyers up to £425k; new Help to Buy; CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants; complete leasehold reform; renters’ reform with Section 21 abolition alongside court changes.
- £20m endowments for 105 towns; extend Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports and zones; Backing Drivers Bill (ban road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, local referendums for 20mph/LTNs); extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.

Food, rural and coastal
- Increase UK-wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament with inflation protection; legal food security target; 50% public food spend local/higher-standard; fast-track farm infrastructure; seasonal worker scheme with taper; £100m Seafood Fund successor; expand inshore opportunities; major flood defence investment.

Union and devolution
- Protect internal market and unfettered trade; extend UK-wide funds and investment zones; specific transport, energy, and industry projects across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland; support for Windsor Framework implementation and legacy bodies.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
